title.narrative: Multi-Sectoral Emergency Response to IDPs, Returnees and Host communities in contested areas Tselemti/West Telemt, Mai Tsebri Town and Lalay Tselemti/Dima Woredas

description.narrative: ltpgtASDEPO propose for a multi-sectoral emergency response project to address the dire and unmet needs of communities at contested locations in the contested areas tonbspbe implemented for 12 months period. The three Woredas/locations (Tselemti/West Telemt, Lalay Tselemti/East Telemt and Maitsebri Town) are among the areas that are significantly affected by the northern conflict and protracted displacement and limited support from the development actors. Based on the Multi-sectoral Inter agency Rapid assessment conducted in August 2024, currently also the communities in these locations are suffering from the lastingnbspeffects of the recent war as well as significantly affected service providing institutions. As indicated in the particular assessment results,nbspmany of the health facilities are partially or fullynbspdamaged and the service provision in these health facilities is challenged by shortage of supplies and equipment along with very few professionals available in these facilities. Accordingly, this proposed project in will address the unmet needs of the communities in the three target locations. Accordingly, under the health intervention the project will deploy MHN team at Lalay Tselemti/East Telemt to provide a health service to communities affected by the crisis. The health intervention will undertake different activities including restoration of 6 damaged health facilities (1 Hospital, 3 Health centers and 2 health posts), building local capacities through training and coaching as well as provide logistics support to the health system in the three target locations. A total of 56,896 individuals from the three target locations planned to be addressed by the health intervention out of which 54% are females and 58% are children. The Nutrition intervention will be implemented only in Tselemti/West Telemt Woreda and it will be coordinated with the existing service that ASDEPO is rendering. The nutrition sector also will strengthen the local system and it will engage in nutritionnbspscreening, treatment and nutrition relatednbspbehavioral change activities. There will also be a nutrition focused cash support to households with children who are malnourished in consultation with the local health and other offices. The nutrition intervention at Tselemti/West Telemt Woreda will address a total of 27,512 individuals of which 51% are females and 90% will be children. The third sector under this project will be Protection which will mainly undertake activities related to cash support to individuals and households under protection risk including children, women, elderly and PWDs.nbspThe multipurpose cash support will include GBV survivors and other vulnerable women, girls and children identified and referred bynbspother protection actorsnbspfor further assistance, enuring complementarity of responses in the target woreda.nbspA total of 2200 individuals in 400 households will be addressed through cash intervention in 3 rounds and 57% of them will be women and 42% will be children. In total, the project under the three intervention sectors will address 60,433 individuals out of which 52% will be females and 58% will be children. 200 PWDs also are planned to be addressed under the project,nbspand more priority willnbspbe given to address their specific needs. The project implementation will actively engage in coordination platforms and staff will be well oriented to familiarize them with the working environment and code of conducts. ASDEPO will ensure that the necessary AAP and protection related procedures are in place while conducting the activities and collaboration with other partners including government offices will be maintained.lt/pgt
